title: is_available is an informal convention off the Attestor trait, with inconsistent receiver
description:
Every attestor exposes an availability probe, but it is not on the `Attestor` trait (persona-attestors/src/lib.rs:108-136), so nothing enforces it:

- `SshAgentAttestor::is_available()` — associated fn (ssh.rs:32)
- `DidKeyAttestor::is_available()` — associated fn (did_key.rs:23)
- `GpgAttestor::is_available()` — associated fn (gpg.rs:22)
- `Fido2Attestor::is_available()` — associated fn (fido2.rs:32)
- `GoaAttestor::is_available()` — associated fn (goa.rs:27)
- `PivAttestor::is_available()` — associated fn (piv.rs:25)
- `TailscaleAttestor::is_available(&self)` — takes `&self` (tailscale.rs:28), because it reads `self.socket_path`
- `OidcCachedAttestor` — has none at all

Consequences today, all visible in registry.rs:19-93:
1. The probe list is hand-maintained. `probe_sources` must special-case Tailscale (`let ts = ...; if ts.is_available()`) against everything else (`if Foo::is_available()`), and special-case OIDC with a comment explaining why it is pushed unconditionally. A ninth attestor added tomorrow compiles fine and is silently never probed.
2. `freshness()` re-implements the same check in six attestors (ssh.rs:152, did_key.rs:90, gpg.rs:138, goa.rs:70, and inverted in tailscale.rs:113) as `if Self::is_available() { Fresh } else { Unavailable }` — five copies of one line that could be a default method.
3. `is_available` cannot be called through `dyn Attestor`, so the registry is the only place it can ever be used.

Fix: add `fn is_available(&self) -> bool` to the `Attestor` trait (a `&self` method works for all eight; the stateless ones ignore it), and give `freshness` a default impl in terms of it. `probe_sources` then becomes a filter over a list of constructed attestors.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.8 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
